method_notes: PRIMARY SOURCE: ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com) chapter-wise PYQ pages for JEE Main and JEE Advanced Mathematics, downloaded 2026-10-01. Every question there carries its paper label (e.g. 'JEE Main 2025 (Online) 22nd January Morning Shift'), so I counted questions per chapter per year. Coverage check: across all ExamSIDE chapters every Main shift adds up to its full maths paper (30 questions per shift in 2019 and 2021-2024, 25 in 2020 and 2025-2026; one 2026 shift has 24), and every Advanced paper adds up too (2019-2020: 18+18, 2021: 19+19, 2022: 18+18, 2023-2024: 17+17, 2025: 16+16, 2026: 16+18). So these are complete counts, not samples. MAIN by_year = questions in that year / number of B.Tech shifts that year: 2019:16, 2020:16, 2021:26, 2022:23, 2023:24, 2024:20, 2025:19, 2026:19. The shift counts come from the union of shift labels across all chapter pages. This is plain arithmetic on complete counts, so direct chapters are labelled coaching_analysis. Note that 2019-2024 papers had 30 maths questions per shift (5 of 10 numericals optional in 2021-2024), while 2020 and 2025-2026 had 25. Pre-2025 per-shift values are therefore roughly 20% higher for the same share of the paper. MAIN avg_questions_per_shift = weighted mean of the yearly per-shift values, with weight 3 for each of 2024, 2025 and 2026 and weight 1 for each of 2019-2023 (2024-26 = 9/14 = 64% of the weight), because the 2024 syllabus cut removed some topics and 2025 cut the paper to 25 questions. ADVANCED by_year = total questions in Paper 1 + Paper 2 that ExamSIDE files under the chapter. avg_questions = plain mean over the 8 years 2019-2026. Each multi-part paragraph or matching question counts as listed by ExamSIDE (one entry per question number). CHAPTER MAPPING: ExamSIDE merges some chapters that the app splits, so I divided them myself. Every chapter built this way is labelled source_type 'estimate'. (a) Matrices vs Determinants: a question goes to Determinants if its text is about a system of linear equations, consistency, infinitely many/unique/no solutions, or evaluates a determinant written in |array| form. Otherwise it goes to Matrices; that includes det/adj/inverse algebra, which coaching books keep in the Matrices chapter. (b) Limits vs Continuity & Differentiability: a question goes to C&D if its text mentions continuity/discontinuity/(non-)differentiability at points, otherwise to Limits. (c) Probability vs Conditional Probability/Bayes/Random Variables: a question goes to Conditional if its text mentions a random variable, distribution, mean/variance, Bayes cues ('given that', 'was', 'found to be', transfers between bags, telling the truth), independence or binomial; otherwise to Probability. Main splits use automatic keyword rules. For Advanced, I read every 2019-2026 question in these merged chapters and made a few manual corrections; I also split ExamSIDE's single Advanced 'trigonometric functions and equations' chapter into Trig Equations (solution-count/set questions) and Trig Ratios & Identities (everything else, including one 2023 inradius question). Other mappings: Main 'differentiation' = Methods of Differentiation; Advanced 'application-of-integration' = Area Under Curves; Advanced 'mathematical-induction-and-binomial-theorem' = Binomial Theorem. ExamSIDE chapters with no app equivalent were left out: Properties of Triangle, Height & Distance, Mathematical Reasoning, Mathematical Induction. CROSS-CHECKS: (1) PW (pw.live) and Vedantu publish identical JEE Main 2025 Jan/April session chapter totals. They match ExamSIDE closely, e.g. 3D 18/17 vs 16/18; Matrices+Determinants 18/15 vs 19/15; Binomial 11/13 vs 11/13; Probability 12/9 vs 12/9; Sequences 13/13 vs 13/14; Trig Equations 2/5 vs 1/5; Logarithm 1/0 vs 1/0. (2) I counted MathonGo's chapter-wise PDF question banks: Jan 2024 (sum 290 of 300; the Sets & Relations PDF would not download), Apr 2024 (300) and Jan 2026 (250). They agree within about ±3 per session for most chapters (Jan 2026: Sequences 17 vs 17, Area 10 vs 10, Trig Eq 2 vs 2, Matrices+Determinants 16 vs 16, Limits+C&D 11 vs 11). Bigger differences in 2024: Definite Integration (MathonGo 34 vs ExamSIDE 43), Functions (30 vs 22), Limits+C&D (39 vs 28), Matrices/Determinants split (MathonGo 20/21 vs my split 24/16). These come from different chapter classification. (3) For Advanced, Allen's 2023 analysis (Probability 5, Determinant & Matrices 3, Complex 2, ITF 2, Vector 2) matches ExamSIDE 2023. Careers360 has an unlabelled Advanced table (16+18 = 34 questions, which matches the 2026 paper totals) that agrees at the unit level on coordinate geometry (5), differential equations (2), probability+statistics (3) and 3D (2). HIGH_YIELD = true if the chapter is in the top 9 of 31 (about 30%) by Main weighted average (cut-off 1.06 per shift) or has Advanced avg >= 1.75 per year (the 9th-ranked value; ties included). ROI = my judgement in line with common coaching advice (questions per shift relative to how long the chapter takes to learn and how hard it is); it is not taken from a single source. CONFIDENCE mainly reflects the Main numbers: high = ExamSIDE counts agree with PW 2025 and/or MathonGo 2024/2026 counts; medium = combined total confirmed but the split between app chapters is my estimate, or counts are very small; low = keyword split with no second source for the split. Advanced numbers come only from ExamSIDE (spot-checked against Allen 2023 and Careers360), so treat Advanced as medium at best.
uncertainties: Trigonometric Equations (flagged Advanced-only) IS still asked in JEE Main after the 2024 syllabus change. ExamSIDE counts 8 questions in 2024 (20 shifts), 6 in 2025 (19 shifts) and 6 in 2026 (19 shifts), mostly 'number of solutions of ... in [a,b]' questions. PW reports 2 (Jan) + 5 (Apr) for 2025, and MathonGo counted 9 in 2024 and 2 in Jan 2026. That is about 0.3-0.4 per shift. ExamSIDE's Main chapter also contains a few trig-function questions (e.g. max/min), so the true 'equations only' count may be slightly lower.

Logarithms (flagged Advanced-only) still appears in JEE Main, but rarely: ExamSIDE has 0 in 2024, 1 in 2025 (22 Jan morning) and 3 in 2026 (23 Jan evening, 4 Apr evening, 8 Apr evening). PW lists 'Basic Mathematics and Logarithm' 1 (Jan 2025) / 0 (Apr 2025); MathonGo 'Basic of Mathematics' has 1 in Jan 2026. So it is roughly 0.05-0.16 per shift; log manipulation is also used inside many other chapters' questions.
Advanced numbers for Sets and Relations and for Logarithms are null: ExamSIDE has no such Advanced chapter, so any such questions are filed under other chapters and cannot be counted.

Matrices vs Determinants, Limits vs Continuity & Differentiability, and Probability vs Conditional Probability are my keyword-based splits of combined ExamSIDE chapters. The combined totals are reliable (cross-checked); the split is not. Combined Matrices+Determinants is about 1.91 per shift in Main (the joint-highest unit with 3D). Combined Limits+C&D is about 1.36. Combined Probability is about 1.15.

The Probability / Conditional Probability split in Main is the weakest number: much question text is rendered as images or MathML on ExamSIDE, so cues like P(A|B) are invisible to keyword matching. Some Bayes questions may be counted as plain Probability.

Chapter boundaries differ between sources: e.g. a definite-integral question involving a limit, or a vector question set in 3D. Per-chapter counts can differ by 10-30% between ExamSIDE and MathonGo for Definite Integration, Functions and Limits/C&D in 2024.

The 2019-2024 per-shift numbers come from 30-question papers and 2020/2025-2026 from 25-question papers, so per-shift values are not strictly comparable across years without rescaling (I did not rescale).
Main 2026 has 19 shifts (Jan 21-24 and 28, Apr 2, 4, 5, 6 and 8 evening). One 2026 shift (4 April evening) shows only 24 maths questions on ExamSIDE, so a question may be missing or dropped.
Motion's blog (motion.ac.in) labels a table 'Jan 2026 / Apr 2026', but its numbers are identical to PW's 2025 table, so I treated it as mislabelled and did not use it.
Collegedunia's 2022-2026 maths unit table gives only rounded per-shift ranges (e.g. '2-3'). I did not use it for numbers.

Advanced Properties of Triangles (2019:1, 2020:2, 2021:2, 2023:1 on ExamSIDE; Allen says 3 'Solution of Triangles' questions in 2023) has no app chapter, so it is not counted anywhere except one 2023 inradius question that ExamSIDE filed under trigonometry (counted in Trig Ratios).

Advanced trig split (Equations vs Ratios) and the manual Advanced corrections for Limits/C&D (2019 x1, 2020 x2, 2024 x1 moved to C&D), Probability, and Determinants (2019 x1) rely on my reading of question text where formulas were partly missing.
